summary: Strong, safe day: all deal facts checked against Bending Spoons' release and StockTitan, visuals are clean and correct, and it follows the voice and platform rules. One small wording fix on Facebook (customers -> prospects).

posts.notes: Checked: Intuit to Bending Spoons, all-cash, $3.68B enterprise value, close expected early 2027 (Bending Spoons release, Nov 19, 2026). 'Yesterday' is correct for a Nov 20 post. The Heloe description matches founder-notes (deals/business changes, verified at search time, AI advice on whether/how/when). 1,250 chars, hook within the first 210, ends with a question, and the 3 hashtags (broad/niche/pillar) come from hashtags.json. Checked: $3.68B (Bending Spoons release) and $12B paid in 2021 (StockTitan says $12.0B, agreed Sep 13, 2021 and closed Nov 1, 2021; it also notes that both are enterprise values, so the comparison is like for like). 242 chars, no hashtag, no link, makes sense without the image. Neutral, does not mock the price drop.

issues: Clarity: 'If your customers run on Mailchimp' reads as the seller's existing customers. The advice (don't blast, track the accounts, reach out when something changes) is about prospects, and matches li-1's 'If you sell to Mailchimp users'. Emailing your own existing customers about a vendor change is a different and often reasonable act, so the current wording blurs the lesson. One-word fix.

fix.text:
An acquisition is a sales signal. Just not on announcement day.

Yesterday Intuit agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons, with closing expected in early 2027. If your prospects run on Mailchimp, it's tempting to email all of them this week.

We'd wait. Announcement day is the noisiest moment, and every vendor has the same headline.

Track those accounts instead, and reach out when something actually changes for that team.

#SalesSignals #Outbound

https://heloe.io/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=organic&utm_content=2026-11-20-fb-1
